statement: Canonical pre-effect authority and admissibility semantics are inherited and frozen.
Pre-effect governed refusal may produce zero governed economic effect.
Post-effect resolution cannot assume that no economic mutation occurred.
A compensation execution is a distinct consequential execution event.
A reversal execution is distinct from the originating execution.
Economic terminal-state equivalence does not imply historical-state identity.
Reconciled state does not automatically imply preserved continuity.
Post-effect indeterminacy must remain distinct from zero effect.
